speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I see you've been experiencing episodes of dizziness and vertigo. To help me understand what's happening, can you describe if these episodes are triggered by changes in your head position, such as rolling over in bed or looking up?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that clear description; the position-dependent nature strongly suggests a benign etiology. Have you noticed any new hearing loss, tinnitus, or ringing in the ears during these spells, or any imbalance while walking? Please also tell me if you have experienced any neurological symptoms like double vision, slurred speech, or weakness.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Audiogram to confirm baseline hearing loss and rule out auditory neuropathy associated with Meniere's disease.

Do you have any history of heart disease, high blood pressure, or diabetes?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Audiometry findings show bilateral high-frequency sensorineural hearing loss consistent with presbycusis. No sudden drops in hearing indicative of Meniere's disease or auditory neuropathy.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)
